PullRequest.Title: chat sticky scroll: more fluid, less vertical space
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A sticky-row position write was immediately followed by offsetHeight on each push-out scroll update, forcing browser style/layout work in the input-to-frame path.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Sticky-scroll push-out could become visibly less fluid because each scroll update synchronously resolved layout before painting.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Sticky row heights are measured when the sticky state is rendered and cached; per-scroll root-height updates consume that cache, removing the synchronous DOM geometry read from the scroll/push-out critical path.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: StickyScrollController registers update() on view.onDidScroll; when the last sticky row is pushed out, StickyScrollWidget.setState first writes the row's style.top and then calls updateRootHeight(). In the base revision getRootHeight() synchronously read lastStickyElement.offsetHeight at line 1831, creating a write-then-layout-read cycle on successive scroll events. The changed line 1874 now obtains the already measured/capped height from _previousElementHeights via getRenderedNodeHeight instead of querying DOM geometry.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scrolling a workbench tree while sticky ancestors are visible or being pushed out
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The scroll event synchronously runs StickyScrollController.update(), computes at most the configured sticky ancestor count, and updates the sticky widget before the frame can paint. The PR adds cached source-range state and class updates but removes the prior offsetHeight read from this critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scroll event frequency and up to seven sticky ancestors; work remains bounded independently of total tree size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread scroll handler; no queue or parallel work. Sticky nodes are bounded by stickyScrollMaxItemCount (default 7).
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rendered sticky heights are now cached in _previousElementHeights and reused on warm scroll updates; the cache is rebuilt on sticky rerender and cleared when hidden. No negative-cache behavior is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the scroll listener, bounded ancestor traversal, DOM writes, and replacement of the per-scroll offsetHeight read are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame-time savings depends on browser style invalidation and tree renderer complexity, but no diff-introduced scaling regression was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed general tree path adds bounded bookkeeping and removes a synchronous geometry read from the push-out scroll path; the latter was recorded as a regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scrolling a chat transcript with experimental tree sticky-scroll enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each scroll synchronously resolves one sticky request, consults cached request-content/source-range state, and updates one sticky row because chat sets stickyScrollMaxItemCount to 1. Initial or invalidated geometry is refreshed on a requestAnimationFrame rather than measured on every scroll.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scroll frequency, one active sticky request, and the number of currently rendered request templates during a coalesced range refresh rather than the full transcript.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One UI-thread sticky update per scroll; source-range refreshes are coalesced by MutableDisposable to one pending animation-frame callback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Request content eligibility is cached by request id/content key; measured source ranges are cached by request id, cleared on view-model change or width change, and rejected ranges use an explicit null negative cache. Initial unseen requests use an estimated range until rendered/measured.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: source provider calls, map lifecycle, rAF coalescing, and the one-row chat bound are explicit in the changed code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long transcripts retain small per-request cache entries while the view model lives, but those entries scale with an already-retained transcript and do not establish substantial incremental memory growth.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. Geometry reads occur only during coalesced range refreshes, not per scroll, and effective sticky cardinality is one.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat resize, input-height change, configuration toggle, theme update, or explicit rerender
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatListWidget lays out the virtual tree and renderer, refreshes sticky state, or rerenders the single sticky row. Width changes clear source ranges and schedule one animation-frame measurement of currently rendered request templates.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Viewport-visible request rows on width invalidation, with one sticky row rendered in chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread layout followed by at most one coalesced animation-frame refresh; repeated scheduling replaces the prior pending callback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm same-width layouts retain source ranges; width changes invalidate them. Configuration changes invalidate negative entries and tree enablement owns controller creation/disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: layout/rerender call flow and coalescing are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of visible request templates varies with viewport and row heights, but virtualization bounds it and these events are much less frequent than scrolling/render frames.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added refresh work is bounded, coalesced where geometry is needed, and tied to resize/configuration/rerender events rather than unbounded transcript history.

Scenarios.Scenario: Prompt timeline flyout and sessions-window sticky request styling
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CSS stacking and class-dependent styling are applied during normal browser style/render processing; no changed JavaScript boundary blocks interaction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single prompt timeline rail and at most one chat sticky row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser rendering only; no explicit asynchronous work or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is used on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changes are CSS and a local configuration predicate with no transitive external operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style cost is not measured, but selectors apply to a small fixed set of sticky/timeline elements.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression established; changed selectors and z-index rules operate on bounded DOM surfaces.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 17 changed files and all diff pages. Traced tree scrolling, chat sticky-source measurement/caching, layout/rerender/configuration paths, and prompt-timeline styling; no actionable diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold. Recorded the removal of the prior per-scroll offsetHeight layout read as a concrete regression fix.
